extracted.intended_audience: funders, program officers, grant reviewers, research administrators, and meta-researchers studying peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Synthesis of empirical criteria used in grant peer review; identifies nine core assessment domains, lists common sub-criteria, reports on inconsistent application and weighting, and gives recommendations for rubric design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the call for proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit with the funder's strategic priorities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed work aligns with the specific aims, themes, or priorities set out in the funding call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical value of the proposed research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the extent to which results will be applicable, actionable, or valuable to stakeholders, policy, practice, or further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (domain)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how the research question fills a gap, challenges existing knowledge, or introduces a new perspective. Note that 'originality' is often vaguely defined in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research question (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly judge whether the central question being asked is new or addresses an unexplored area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel theoretical framework (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project uses or develops an original theoretical approach or perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel population studied (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the study targets populations, contexts, or samples that have been under-studied or are new to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of known elements in new way (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination of known elements in new way
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize innovation that arises from novel recombination of existing concepts, methods, or datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovativeness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish methodological or conceptual innovations from mere incremental changes; judge whether the approach advances practice or enables new types of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (domain)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the overall study design for soundness and fit to the question; consider internal and external validity, analytic plans, and quality controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal validity / design rigor (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the design minimizes bias and supports causal or reliable inference (controls, randomization, blinding where appropriate, clear protocols).

rubrics_metrics.name: External validity / generalizability (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how well findings are likely to generalize beyond the study sample or setting; consider sampling strategy and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical / analytical plan (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity, appropriateness, and rigor of proposed analyses, including handling of confounders, modelling choices, and reproducibility considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance procedures (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for processes to ensure data integrity, protocol adherence, monitoring, and reproducible workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit power/sample size calculations or rationale demonstrating that planned sample is sufficient for objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility (domain)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the realism of timing, resources, and team capacity relative to proposed tasks; include assessment of risks and contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic timeline (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether milestones and overall schedule are achievable given scope and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record on similar projects (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider investigators' prior experience delivering comparable work as evidence of likely success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource availability (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that necessary data sources, equipment, infrastructure, and personnel are available or accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk mitigation plan (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for identification of project risks and concrete contingency strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data showing approach works (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value pilot results or preliminary evidence that supports feasibility and chosen methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy and justification of requested resources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the budget is appropriate, justified, and sufficient to deliver the project objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether expected benefits/outcomes are reasonable given proposed costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear line-item justification linking costs to project activities and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value-for-money (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider overall return on investment, prioritizing projects that deliver strong outcomes per funding unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of personnel costs (sub-criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge personnel salaries and FTEs against norms and whether staffing is appropriate for tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with ethical norms; ethical implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess human/animal research protections, data ethics, consent, potential harms, and broader ethical implications of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing of the grant application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate readability and clarity; note that 'writing quality' is explicitly used as a criterion and correlates with scores, which may advantage applicants with more polish or native English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion application consistency (meta-finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria are inconsistently applied across reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may interpret and weight criteria differently; consider measures to detect and reduce inter-reviewer variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable weighting of criteria (meta-finding)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some reviewers give equal weight to all criteria, others emphasize one or two; inconsistency in weighting affects fairness and comparability of scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and methodology often weighted highest (meta-finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and methodology are most commonly weighted highest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These domains frequently dominate reviewer judgments and overall scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vagueness of criteria (meta-finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many criteria are vague — 'originality' rarely has operational definition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vague terms increase subjectivity; operational definitions reduce ambiguity and improve reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define each criterion clearly (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should clearly define each criterion to reduce subjectivity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational definitions and examples for terms like 'originality', 'innovative', or 'impact' to guide reviewers toward consistent interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify weights for criteria (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should specify weights rather than leaving weighting to reviewer discretion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit weightings or scoring guidance to make relative importance of domains transparent and to standardize scoring across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train reviewers on operational definitions (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should train reviewers on operational definitions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide calibration exercises, exemplars, or reviewer training to align interpretations and scoring behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor consistency of criterion application (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should monitor consistency of criterion application across reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement quality assurance (e.g., inter-rater reliability checks, audits, statistical monitoring) and feedback loops to detect and correct inconsistent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design defensible rubrics (implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A defensible rubric should explicitly enumerate, define, and weight each criterion it uses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct rubrics based on the nine-domain structure as a comprehensive consensus; document definitions, weights, and scoring instructions to support fairness and defensibility.
